身外減法門・Subtraction from the Body

     減法根源必要知，即同求一一般推，                    The root of the subtraction method you
     呼如身下須當減，言十從身本位除。                    must know;
                                         It is like the “seeking unity” method applied;
身外減法者，除法之捷術也，與身外加法相反。其法以實                When “as-is” is called, subtract below the
為身，於身外逐位減之，呼如減下身位，言十從身本位除。               body;
凡十問。                                     When ten is reached, divide from the body
                                         itself.

                                    The “subtraction from the body” method is the in-
                                    verse of the addition method: it performs division by
                                    subtracting from the dividend itself. “As-is” means
                                    subtract below the current digit; “ten” means sub-
                                    tract from the current digit itself. This is a stream-
                                    lined division technique on the counting board.

即得。                                 Method: Place the cash above as dividend; use the
                                    dou-price as divisor; subtract from the body from
                                    above; obtain.
                                    (Calculation: 4,320 ÷ 20 = 216)

九歸除法門・Division by the Nine Returns

     實少法多從法歸，實多滿法進前居，                     When the dividend is small and divisor
     常存除數專心記，法實相停九十餘。                     large, follow the return method;
     但遇無除還頭位，然將釋九數呼除，                     When the dividend fills the divisor, advance
     流傳故泄真消息，求一穿韜總不如。                     to the next position;
                                          Keep the divisor always in mind;
九歸除法者，以九歸訣為除法之要術也。實少於法，則從                 When divisor and dividend match, the re-
法歸之；實多於法，則進位而居之。常記除數於心，法實                 mainder is in the nineties.
相等則餘九十餘。凡二十九問。                            When a digit cannot be divided, return to
                                          the head position;
                                          Then use the nine-explanations method to
                                          call the division;
                                          This tradition reveals the true secret;
                                          The “seeking unity” method cannot com-
                                          pare.

                                     The “nine returns” division uses the division rhymes
                                     given in the General Principles. When the dividend
                                     is smaller than the divisor, use the “return” method;
                                     when the dividend is larger, advance the quotient.
                                     The practitioner must memorize the divisor and keep
                                     it in mind. When the division is exact, the remainder
                                     is in the nineties. If a digit cannot be divided, return
                                     to the head position and use the “nine explanations”
                                     method. This method, though not the orthodox ap-
                                     proach (商除), is easier for beginners.
Suanxue Qimeng ・Bilingual Edition                                                     16

折變互差門・Conversion and Mutual Difference

     折變互差要詳知，多少相乘作實推，                         For conversion and mutual difference, you
     以少求多因作母，除來便見兩無虧。                         must know in detail;
                                              Multiply the quantities to make the divi-
折變互差者，以物易物、以多變少之法也。其法以所求率                     dend;
與所有數相乘為實，以所知率為法除之，得所求之數。凡                     To seek more from less, use multiplication
十五問。                                          as the base;
                                              Divide and see that nothing is lost.

                                         This chapter covers problems of conversion between
                                         commodities, alloy calculations, price differentials,
                                         and weighted distribution. These problems involve
                                         multiple steps of multiplication and division, often
                                         with fractional rates.

Appendix: Technical Notes ・附錄：技術說明
一、算籌記數法                                                       I. Counting Rod Notation (算籌記數法)
中國古代以算籌記數，縱橫相間，以別位值。一縱十橫，                                     Ancient Chinese mathematics used counting rods (算
百立千僵。算籌以竹為之，長約三寸，徑約一分。記數之                                     籌) made of bamboo, approximately 3 inches long,
法：一至四以縱置之，五以一橫置之，六至九以橫五加縱                                     arranged on a counting board. The notation alter-
數置之。十位則一橫十縱，百位復為縱，千位復為橫，以                                     nates between vertical and horizontal orientations
此相間。此訣所謂「一縱十橫，百立千僵」也。                                         by place value: units vertical, tens horizontal, hun-
二、增乘開方法                                                       dreds vertical, thousands horizontal. Digits 1–4 are
增乘開方者，以漸進之法求方程之根也。其法置積為實，                                     represented by 1–4 rods in the appropriate orienta-
立初商，以次乘實，遞減求之。賈憲首創此術，朱世傑廣                                     tion; 5 is a single horizontal bar (for units) or ver-
而用之，以解高次方程。此法與西洋之魯菲尼—霍納法相                                     tical bar (for tens); 6–9 combine the 5-bar with 1–4
合，而早於西洋數百年。                                                   additional rods. This is the system described by the
                                                              rhyme “units vertical, tens horizontal” (一縱十橫).
三、天元術
天元術者，以天元一為未知數，立方程而求解之術也。其                                     II. Incremental Root Extraction (增乘開方法)
法以「太」字標常數項，以元之冪次遞降排列。李冶首創                                     The “incremental multiplication” method for root ex-
於《測圓海鏡》，朱世傑繼之於《四元玉鑑》
                   ，並推廣為四                                     traction was developed by Jia Xian (11th century) and
元術。此為中國代數學之最高成就。                                              extended by Zhu Shijie. It systematically extracts
                                                              roots digit by digit through a process of successive
四、本書流傳
                                                              approximation. This method is algebraically equiva-
算學啓蒙成書於元大德三年（1299 年）
                   ，在中國久已失傳。
                                                              lent to the Ruffini–Horner method developed in Eu-
清初始從朝鮮發現，道光十九年（1839 年）揚州羅士琳
                                                              rope centuries later.
重刻之。此書東傳日本，影響和算之發展甚大。
                                                              III. The Tian Yuan Method (天元術)
                                                              The “celestial element” method uses tian yuan yi (天
                                                              元一, “celestial element one”) as the unknown vari-
                                                              able. Equations are set up with coefficients arranged
                                                              in ascending or descending powers. Li Ye (李冶) pio-
                                                              neered this in his Ce Yuan Hai Jing (測圓海鏡, 1248);
                                                              Zhu Shijie extended it to the si yuan (四 元, “four
                                                              elements”) method for systems of equations in his
                                                              Siyuan Yujian (四元玉鑑, 1303).
                                                              IV. Transmission of the Text
                                                              The Suanxue Qimeng was written in 1299 and was
                                                              lost in China for centuries. A Korean edition was re-
                                                              discovered in the early Qing dynasty. Luo Shilin (羅
                                                              士琳) republished it in Yangzhou in 1839. The work
                                                              profoundly influenced the development of wasan (和
                                                              算, Japanese mathematics).

  此門論方田、直田、勾股田、圭田、梯田、圓      This chapter treats the calculation of areas for fields
田諸形段之面積計算。一畝等於二百四十平方步， of various geometric shapes: square fields, rectangular
為畝法。                   fields, right-triangle fields, wedge-shaped fields, trape-
  凡田面之廣從相乘，為積步；以畝法二百四 zoidal fields, and circular fields. The standard conversion
十步除之，得畝數。如有零步，以畝法折之為分、 is 1 mu = 240 square bu.
厘、毫。                        In general: multiply the width by the length to obtain
                       the area in square bu; divide by the mu-factor of 240 to
                       obtain the number of mu. Any remainder is converted to
                       fen, li, and hao.

                       the area?

                       A: 38 mu and 4 fen.

                       completes the problem.

窖為方錐臺，囤為圓柱體。斛法一尺六寸二分，即 circular  granaries. A granary (cang) is a rectangular prism;

  凡積粟之術，先求其容積，以斛法除之，即得 (dun) is a cylinder. The hu-factor is 1.62 cubic chi, i.e., the

                           The general method: first find the volume, then di-

3 Chapter 3 / 第三門：雙據互換門 — Double Proportion Problems
雙據互換門 六問               Double Proportion Problems 6 Problems
  此門論重今有之術，凡數經互換而得其平。以      This chapter treats the method of double proportion
所求率乘所有數，以所有率為法除之，為今有術。 (zhong  jinyou). When quantities are related through mul-
重今有者，再乘再除也。            tiple intermediate proportions, we apply successive mul-
                       tiplication and division. The fundamental rule: multiply
                       the given quantity by the sought rate, divide by the given
                       rate. Double proportion applies this process twice.

Problem 26 / 第二十六問：絹價 — Silk Price                     Problem 26 / 第二十六問：絹價 — Silk Price
問：今有絹一疋，價鈔二貫五百文，問丈價幾何？ Q: Now there is one bolt of silk, price 2 guan 500 wen.
                       What is the price per zhang?
答曰：每丈六百二十五文。
                       A: 625 wen per zhang.
術曰：列鈔二貫五百文，以四丈除之，得六百二
十五文，合問。                Method: Place the money of 2 guan 500 wen, divide by 4
                       zhang to obtain 625 wen. This completes the problem.

The standard bolt (疋) of silk = 4 zhang, so price per zhang = 2500 ÷ 4 = 625 wen.

4 Chapter 4 / 第四門：求差分和門 — Sum-and-Difference Problems
求差分和門 九問                                             Sum-and-Difference Problems 9 Problems
  此門論和差之術。已知二數之和與差，或和與                                   This chapter treats the method of sum and difference.
較，求二數各若干。術云：并兩數為和，相減為                                Given the sum and difference of two numbers, find each
差。和加差而半之，為大數；和減差而半之，為                                number. The method says: adding the two numbers gives
小數。                                                  the sum; subtracting gives the difference. Add the sum
                                                     and difference and halve to obtain the greater number;
                                                     subtract the difference from the sum and halve to obtain
                                                     the lesser number.

7 Chapter 7 / 第七門：貴賤反率門 — Inverse Proportion (Price/Rate)
貴賤反率門 八問               Inverse Proportion (Price/Rate) 8 Problems
  此門論反率之術，凡物有貴賤，以價之貴賤      This chapter treats the method of inverse proportion.
為率之反。價貴則物少，價賤則物多，故曰反率。 When   goods have high and low prices, the rates are in-
以貴價乘賤物，以賤價乘貴物，各得共價。    versely proportional to the prices. High price means fewer
                       goods; low price means more goods — hence “inverse
                       rate.” Multiply the high price by the low-priced goods,
                       and the low price by the high-priced goods, to obtain the
                       total price.

9 Chapter 8 / 第八門：開方釋鎖門 — Root Extraction and Lock-Releasing
開方釋鎖門 十六問              Root Extraction and Lock-Releasing 16 Problems
  開方者，求平方根、立方根之法也。釋鎖者，     “Root extraction” (kaifang) refers to the method of
層層解脫，如開鎖然。其術列實於中，借一算子， finding square roots and cube roots. “Lock-releasing”
超位進之，商所得之數，以除實，層層遞減，直 (shisuo) means layer-by-layer release, like unlocking a
至實盡為止。                 lock. The method: place the dividend (shi) in the center,
                       borrow a counting rod, advance it by superposition, esti-
                       mate the quotient, divide the dividend, and reduce layer
                       by layer until the dividend is exhausted.

10 Chapter 9 / 第九門：盈不足術門 — Excess and Deficit Method
盈不足術門 九問                                           Excess and Deficit Method 9 Problems
  盈不足術者，假設兩次試算，一盈一不足，或                                 The method of excess and deficit (ying buzu): make
兩盈、兩不足，以求未知數之法也。以盈不足之                              two trial assumptions, one excess (ying) and one deficit
數，各乘所設之率，相減為實；又以盈不足相減                              (buzu), or both excess or both deficit, to find the unknown.
為法；除之得數。                                           Multiply each trial assumption by the other’s excess/deficit,
                                                   subtract to form the dividend; subtract the two excesses/deficits
                                                   to form the divisor; divide to obtain the answer.

Problem 77 / 第七十七問：買物盈不足 — Buying                  Problem 77 / 第七十七問：買物盈不足 — Buying Goods
Goods Excess and Deficit                           Excess and Deficit
問：今有買物，人出八，盈三；人出七，不足四， Q: Now for buying goods: if each person contributes 8,
問人數物價各幾何？              there is an excess of 3; if each contributes 7, there is a
                       deficit of 4. How many people and what is the price of
答曰：人七，物價五十三。
                       the goods?
術曰：置盈三、不足四，并之，得七，為人數；以
                       A: 7 people; price of goods: 53.
人七乘出八，得五十六；內減盈三，得五十三，為
物價；又以人七乘出七，得四十九；加不足四，亦 Method: Place the excess 3 and deficit 4, add them to
得五十三，合問。               obtain 7 as the number of people; multiply 7 people by

                       problem.

Modern: Let n = people, P = price. 8n = P + 3; 7n = P − 4. Subtracting: n = 7, so P = 8(7) − 3 = 53.

12 Chapter 11 / 第十一門：天元如積門 — The Celestial Element Method
天元如積門 十八問               The Celestial Element Method 18 Problems
  天元術者，中國古代代數之最高成就也。立       The tian yuan (Celestial Element) method represents
天元一為所求之數，依題意列如積式，正負相消，  the highest  achievement of medieval Chinese algebra. One
得開方式，開方求之，即得所求。朱世傑以此術 establishes tian yuan yi (Celestial Element One) as the
通貫全書，由淺入深，示學者以代數之津梁。    unknown, constructs a “product-equalization” (ruji) equa-
                    、天 tion according to the problem, eliminates positive and
  天元式之排列，自上而下：太極（常數項）
元（一次）、天元平方（二次）
             、天元立方（三次）， negative terms to obtain an “open-form” equation, and
以算籌縱橫布之。                extracts roots to solve. Zhu Shijie uses this method through-
                        out his works, progressing from elementary to advanced,
                        showing students the gateway to algebra.
                            The tian yuan arrangement runs from top to bottom:
                        the taiji (constant term), tian yuan (linear term), tian yuan
                        square (quadratic), tian yuan cube (cubic), laid out with
                        counting rods in vertical and horizontal patterns.

13 Historical and Mathematical Commentary / 歷史與數學評述
天元術之歷史意義               Historical Significance of the Tian Yuan Method
  天元術為中國代數學之巔峰。朱世傑以此法      The tian yuan method represents the pinnacle of Chi-
解多項式方程，由一次直至四次，開中國代數之  nese  medieval algebra. Zhu Shijie used this method to
先河。其法以「太」記常數項，「元」記一次項， solve polynomial equations from degree 1 through de-
自上而下列高次項，以縱橫算籌表示正負，形成 gree 4, pioneering Chinese algebraic symbolism. The method
獨特之位值記數系統。             uses “tai” to mark the constant term, “yuan” for the linear
 《算學啟蒙》三卷，循序漸進：卷上明基礎運 term, with higher powers arranged below, using verti-
算，卷中演分數比例，卷下闡方程天元。全書二 cal and horizontal counting rods to indicate positive and
百五十九問，涵蓋算術、代數、幾何之要領，實 negative, forming a unique place-value system.
為十三世紀中國數學之百科全書。            The three volumes of Suanxue Qimeng progress sys-
                       tematically: Volume I covers basic operations, Volume II
                       develops fractions and proportions, and Volume III presents
                       equations and the celestial element. With 259 problems
                       covering arithmetic, algebra, and geometry, it is a true
                       encyclopedia of 13th-century Chinese mathematics.

   主要術法總結：                               Summary of Main Methods:

   1. 今有術：以所求率乘所有數，以所有率為法                1. Rule of Three (Jinyou): Multiply the given quan-
      除之。                                   tity by the sought rate; divide by the given rate.
   2. 衰分術：各列其衰，并而為法，以所分乘未                2. Proportional Distribution (Shuai fen): List each
      并者，實如法而一。                             ratio, add to form the divisor; multiply the quantity
   3. 盈不足術：盈不足相并為人數，盈不足相減                   by each uncombined ratio; divide.
      為物價差。                              3. Excess and Deficit (Ying buzu): Add excess and
   4. 方程術：以正負入之，直除消元，互乘求對。                  deficit for the number of people; subtract for price
   5. 天元術：立天元一為未知數，如積列式，開                   differences.
      方求之。                               4. Equation Method (Fangcheng): Use positive and
   6. 開方術：借一算，超位進之，商除層層遞減。                  negative numbers; eliminate variables by direct di-
                                            vision and cross-multiplication.
                                         5. Celestial Element (Tian yuan): Establish tian yuan
                                            yi as the unknown; set up the product equation;
                                            extract roots.
                                         6. Root Extraction (Kaifang): Borrow a rod, advance

Contents / िवषयािन
 1. Daśagitika (दशगीितका) — 33 verses
    Numerical notation, planetary periods, sine table, astronomical constants

 2. Ganitapada (गिणतपादः) — 33 verses
    Mathematics: squares, cubes, areas, volumes, shadows, kuṭtaka

 3. Kalakriyapada (कालिक्रयापादः) — 25 verses
    Time reckoning: yugas, months, days, planetary motion

 4. Golapada (गोलपादः) — 50 verses
    Spherical astronomy: Earth as sphere, eclipses, stellar positions




                           Key Mathematical Contributions
                           Value of π ≈ 3.1416                   Verse 2.10
                           24-fold sine table (jya)              Verses 1.12, 2.11–12
                           Kuṭtaka (pulverizer) method           Verses 2.32–33
                           Earth’s rotation on its axis          Golapada 9

Preface / प्रस्तावना
आयर्भटीयम् इदं ग्रन्थं समुद्रमथन, रासलीला,              The Aryabhatiya is the fundamental text of
ब्रह्महत्यादीनां रहस्यं ज्ञातुं शक्यते । इदं प्राचीनं   ancient Indian astronomy and mathemat-
भारतीयं ज्योितषशास्त्रस्य गिणतस्य च                     ics. Composed by Aryabhata in 499 CE
मूलग्रन्थः।                                             when he was but 23 years old, this trea-
                                                        tise consists of 121 verses divided into four
                                                        chapters (pādas).


प्रत्ये कपादे सूक्तयः सं युक्ताः गिणतज्योितषयोः         Each pāda contains verses giving complete
सम्पूणर्ं ज्ञानं ददित। इदं सम्पादनं दे वनागिरिलप्यां    knowledge of mathematics and astronomy.
मूलसं स्कृतं आङ्ग्लानुवादे न सह प्रस्तौित।              The present edition presents the original
                                                        Sanskrit in Devanagari script alongside an
                                                        English translation, with IAST translitera-
                                                        tion of key terms.

First Chapter: Dasagitika / प्रथमः पादः -- दशगीितका
प्रथम आयर्भटीय पद्धित दशगीितका नाम।                           The first method of the Aryabhatiya is
��दश''         सं ख्यावाचक,   ��गीितका''                      called Daśagītikā. “Daśa” is a numeri-
गानयोग्यसूत्रािण।           दशाक्षररिचतत्वे न                 cal term, and “gītikā” means verses fit for
दशगीितकेत्युच्यते ।                                           singing. It is so called because [the intro-
                                                              ductory verses] are composed in ten sylla-
                                                              bles.

Verse 1 — Invocation / मङ्गलाचरण
     ब्रह्मा नारायणो ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मा वे धाः सनातनः ।             Brahmā nārāyaṇo brahmā brahmā
     परमे ष्ठी च सप्तै ते मुनयः स्युः पुरःसराः ॥ १ ॥             vedhāḥ sanātanaḥ.
                                                                 Parameṣṭhī ca saptaite munayaḥ
                                                                 syuḥ puraḥsarāḥ. [1]
                                                                 Brahma, Narayana, Brahma, Brahma, Ved-
                                                                 has the Eternal, and Parameshthin—these
                                                                 seven sages are the foremost leaders. [1]


Verse 2 — Numerical Notation / सं ख्यास्थानकल्पना
     वगार्क्षरािण कादीिन नव ताण्डाक्षरािण च ।                    Vargākṣarāṇi      kādīni     nava
     नव धनािन चै तािन स्थानान्यष्टादश स्मृतम् ॥ २ ॥              tāṇḍākṣarāṇi ca.
                                                                 Nava dhānāni caitāni sthānn̄yaṣṭā-
                                                                 daśa smr̄tam. [2]
                                                                 The varga letters beginning with ka are
                                                                 nine in number; the avarga letters are also
                                                                 nine. Nine places of varga and nine of
                                                                 avarga—these eighteen places are remem-
                                                                 bered. [2]
                                                                 [Explanatory note: Aryabhata’s alpha-
                                                                 betic numerical notation assigns values to
                                                                 consonants: ka-ta-pa-ya = 1-25, and to
                                                                 vowels representing powers of 10.]


Verse 3 — Revolutions of the Sun / सूयर्स्य चतुयर्ुगे भगणाः
     सूयर्स्य भगणा यत्र चतुयर्ुगे यािन्त ते कित ।                Sūryasya bhagānā yatra catur-yuge
     चतुर्िंवशितसहस्रािण षट् शतािन च सप्तितः ॥ ३ ॥               yānti te kati.
                                                                 Catur-viḿsati-sahasrāṇi ṣaṭ-śatāni
                                                                 ca saptatiḥ. [3]
                                                                 The revolutions of the Sun in a Caturyuga
                                                                 are: twenty-four thousand and six hundred
                                                                 and seventy, [that is] 4,320,000. [3]


Verse 4 — Moon’s Revolutions / शिशनो भगणाः
     शिशनो भगणा यत्र पञ्च सप्तितरुत्तरम् ।                       Śaśino bhagānā yatra pañca saptatir
     ित्रसहस्रािण चाष्टौ च लक्षं च द्वे च दिक्षणे ॥ ४ ॥          uttaram.
                                                                 Tri-sahasrāṇi cāṣṭau ca laks̄aṃ ca
                                                                 dve ca dakṣiṇe. [4]
                                                                 The revolutions of the Moon: five and sev-
                                                                 enty above, three thousand and eight, and
                                                                 one hundred-thousand and two on the right
                                                                 [side], [that is] 57,753,336. [4]
Aryabhatiya — Bilingual Edition                                                             5


Verse 5 — Lunar Apogee and Nodes / चन्द्रोच्चराहुभगणौ
    चन्द्रोच्चं शिनमन्दं च राहुकेतू तथै व च ।           Candroccaṃ śani-mandaṃ ca rāhu-
    भगणानां शतं द्वे तु सहस्रािण च सप्तितः ॥ ५ ॥        ketū tathaiva ca.
                                                        Bhagān̄̄anaṃ śataṃ dve tu sahas-
                                                        rāṇi ca saptatiḥ. [5]
                                                        The [apogee] of the Moon, the [apogee]
                                                        of Saturn, and Rahu and Ketu: two hun-
                                                        dred and seventy-thousand [revolutions in
                                                        a Caturyuga]. [5]
                                                        [Explanatory note: Rahu and Ketu are
                                                        the ascending and descending nodes of the
                                                        Moon, responsible for eclipses.]
Aryabhatiya — Bilingual Edition                                                                    6


Verse 6 — The Manus / मनुसङ्ख्या
     चतुदर्श व्यतीताः स्युमर्नवोऽष्टौ तथापराः ।             Caturdaśa vyatīt̄̄ah syur manavo
     प्रवतर्मानश्चै कस्तु कल्पे सप्तदश स्मृताः ॥ ६ ॥        'ṣṭau tathāparāḥ.
                                                            Pravartamānaś caikas tu kalpe sap-
                                                            tadaśa smr̄tāḥ. [6]
                                                            Fourteen Manus have passed away; eight
                                                            are yet to come; and one is current—
                                                            seventeen Manus are remembered in a
                                                            Kalpa. [6]
                                                            [Explanatory note: A Kalpa is one day of
                                                            Brahma, equal to 1000 Caturyugas. Each
                                                            Manu rules over 71 Caturyugas.]


Verse 7 — Signs and Degrees / राश्यं शकल्पना
     द्वादशा सूयर्जः सोऽयं िंत्रशता भािगतो रिवः ।           Dvādaśā sūryajaḥ so'yaṃ triḿśatā
     भागे न ते न रािशः स्यात्तनुं िंत्रशत् गुणीकृतम् ॥ ७    bhāgito raviḥ.
     ॥                                                      Bhāgena tena rāśiḥ syāt tanuṃ
                                                            triḿśat guṇīkr̄tam. [7]
                                                            The Sun, born of the twelve [signs], is di-
                                                            vided by thirty. By that division a sign is
                                                            produced; a degree is [a sign] multiplied by
                                                            thirty. [7]
                                                            [Explanatory note: 12 signs (rāsi) × 30
                                                            degrees = 360◦ in a circle.]


Verse 8 — Measure of the Earth / योजनप्रमाणम्
     योजनं ित्रभवं वृत्तं भूमेयार्े जनलक्षणम् ।             Yojanaṃ tribhavaṃ vr̄ttaṃ bhūmer
     िनराकारः सदा व्यापी शून्यमध्यः सनातनः ॥ ८ ॥            yojana-lakṣaṇam.
                                                            Nirākāraḥ sadā vyāpī śūnyamad-
                                                            hyaḥ sanātanaḥ. [8]
                                                            A yojana: the circle of the Earth has a
                                                            circumference measured in yojanas. [The
                                                            Earth is] formless, always pervading, void
                                                            at the centre, eternal. [8]
                                                            [Explanatory note: The circumference of
                                                            the Earth is given as 4,967 yojanas. 1 yo-
                                                            jana ≈ 7.5 miles.]

Verse 9 — Planetary Orbits / ग्रहकक्ष्याः
     ग्रहाणां कक्ष्यािवस्तारा योजनै स्तै ः प्रकीर्ितताः ।   Grahāṇāṃ kakṣyā-vistārā yojanais
     भूमेरधर्ं ित्रभागश्च व्यासः सूयर्स्य कीर्िततः ॥ ९ ॥    taiḥ prakīrtitāḥ.
                                                            Bhūmer ardhaṃ tribhāgaś ca vyāsaḥ
                                                            sūryasya kīrtitaḥ. [9]
                                                            The diameters of the orbits of the plan-
                                                            ets are proclaimed in yojanas. Half of the
                                                            Earth plus a third: the diameter of the Sun
                                                            is proclaimed. [9]
                                                            [Explanatory note: The Sun’s diameter =
                                                            4410 yojanas; the Moon’s = 315 yojanas;
                                                            Earth’s = 1050 yojanas.]


Verse 10 — The 24 Sines / चतुर्िंवशत्यधर्ज्याः

    ित्रभुजं षट् कोणं वृत्तं षट् िंत्रशदं शेन योजये त् ।   Tribhujaṃ      ṣaṭkoṇaṃ     vr̄ttaṃ
    चतुर्िंवशितजीवाः स्युः सप्तिभः सिहताः क्रमात् ॥        ṣa-triḿśad-aḿśena yojayet.
    १० ॥                                                   Catur-viḿsati-jīvāḥ syuḥ saptabhiḥ
                                                           sahitāḥ kramāt. [10]
                                                           A triangle, a hexagon, and a circle are
                                                           joined by thirty-six degrees. Twenty-four
                                                           chords are produced, each increased suc-
                                                           cessively by seven [and other differences].
                                                           [10]

Second Chapter: Ganitapada / िद्वतीयः पादः -- गिणतपादः
गिणतपादे                                                 In the Ganitapada are treated: squares,
वगर्घनमूलक्षे त्रफलवृत्तजीवाकूट्टकछायािदिवषयाः           cubes, square-roots, cube-roots, areas of
सं स्कृताः।                                              figures, the circle, chords, the pulverizer
                                                         (kuṭtaka), shadows, and related topics.


Verse 1 / मङ्गलाचरणम्
     प्रथमपादक्रमादे व ह्यः प्रणम्य गणे श्वरम् ।            Prathama-pāda-kramād eva hyaḥ
     ततो गिणतमाख्यास्ये गिणतज्ञानमुत्तमम् ॥ १ ॥             praṇamya gaṇeśvaram.
                                                            Tato gaṇitam ākhyāsye gaṇita-
                                                            jñānam uttamam. [1]
                                                            Having bowed to the Lord of Calculation
                                                            (Ganeśvara) in the order of the first chap-
                                                            ter, I shall now expound the science of cal-
                                                            culation, the highest knowledge of mathe-
                                                            matics. [1]


Verse 2 — Place Values / स्थाननामािन
     एकं दश शतं सहस्रमयुतं लक्षं प्रयुतं कोट्यः ।           Ekaṃ daśa śataṃ sahasram ayutaṃ
     अबुर्दं बृन्दमखखवर्ं िनखवर्ं महापद्मं च ॥ २ ॥          lakṣaṃ prayutaṃ koṭyaḥ.
                                                            Arbudaṃ br̄ndam akha-kharvaṃ
                                                            nikharvaṃ mahā-padmaṃ ca. [2]
                                                            One, ten, hundred, thousand, myriads
                                                            (ayuta), lakh (lakṣa), ten-lakhs (prayuta),
                                                            crore (koṭi), ten-crores (arbuda), hundred-
                                                            crores (bnda), thousand-crores (kharva),
                                                            ten-thousand-crores (nikharva), hundred-
                                                            thousand-crores (mahā-padma). [2]
                                                            [Explanatory note: The Indian decimal
                                                            place-value system proceeds in powers of
                                                            10.]
Aryabhatiya — Bilingual Edition                                                                 10


Verse 3 — Square / वगर्ः
    सं युत्यकस्थानसं ज्ञं ततः सप्तदशस्वरे ।              Saṃyuty-aka-sthāna-saj̣ñaṃ tataḥ
    स्वरूपं चै व तत् प्रोक्तं वगर्संज्ञं तथै व च ॥ ३ ॥   saptadaśa-svare.
                                                         Svarūpaṃ caiva tat proktaṃ varga-
                                                         saj̣ñaṃ tathaiva ca. [3]
                                                         The product of a number with itself is
                                                         called the varga [square]. In the odd places
                                                         [the product] is as stated; the square is also
                                                         called “svarūpa” [own-form]. [3]


Verse 4 — Square Root / वगर्मूलम्
    वगर्स्य मूलमाख्यातं यथोक्तं गिणतै ः पुरा ।           Vargasya mūlam ākhyātaṃ yathok-
    सवर्दोषिविनमुर्क्तं िविंध श्रूयतां मया ॥ ४ ॥         taṃ gaṇitaiḥ purā.
                                                         Sarva-doṣa-vinirmuktaṃ   vidhiṃ
                                                         śrūyatāṃ mayā. [4]
                                                         The square root of a square is declared as
                                                         formerly spoken by calculators. Hear from
                                                         me the method free from all defects. [4]
                                                         [Explanatory note: Method: mark off pe-
                                                         riods of two digits from the right. Find the
                                                         largest square in the leftmost period; sub-
                                                         tract and bring down the next period. Dou-
                                                         ble the current root and divide into the re-
                                                         mainder. Repeat.]

Verse 5 — Cube / घनः
    ित्रसमचतुष्कोणं घनं स्यादथवाऽपरम् ।                  Tri-sama-catuṣkoṇaṃ ghanaṃ syād
    त्रयाणां समवृत्तानां समसं योगजं स्मृतम् ॥ ५ ॥        athavāparam.
                                                         Trayāṇām sama-vr̄ttānām sama-
                                                         saṃyogajaṃ smr̄tam. [5]
                                                         A cube is an equi-quadrilateral [solid] with
                                                         three equal dimensions. It is remembered
                                                         as produced from the product of three
                                                         equal quantities. [5]
                                                         [Explanatory note: ghana literally means

Verse 13 — The Pulverizer (Kuṭtaka) / कूट्टकम्
    गुणकारे ण युक्ते ते वजर्ियत्वा तु तद्गण     ु ौ।         Guṇakāreṇa yukte te varjayitvā tu
    िछन्ने तत्र गुणौ ज्ञे यौ कूट्टकं तिद्वदुबुर्धाः ॥ १३ ॥   tad-guṇau.
                                                             Chinne tatra guṇau jñeyāu kuṭṭakaṃ
                                                             tad-vidur budhāḥ. [13]
                                                             The two [quantities], when combined with
                                                             the multiplier, are to be reduced [by the
                                                             greatest common divisor]. When divided,
                                                             the two multipliers are to be known there:
                                                             the wise call this the kuṭtaka [pulverizer].
                                                             [13]
                                                             [Explanatory note: The kuṭtaka (“pulver-
                                                             izer”) is Aryabhata’s method for solving
                                                             linear indeterminate equations of the form
                                                             ax+by = c. It is essentially the Euclidean
                                                             algorithm applied to find solutions to Dio-
                                                             phantine equations.]

The Kuṭtaka Method — Detailed Procedure
    कूट्टकिविधः---भाजकभाज्ययोः परस्परभागदानं कृत्वा          The Kuṭtaka Method:

    गुणकारभाजकौ लभ्ये ते।                                    (bhājya) mutually until the remainder be-
                                                             comes 1. Then by back-substitution, the

                                                             tained.

Verse 1 — Division of Time / कालिवभागः
     नाडी तु दशपञ्चाशत्पलं षष्ट्या तु तै ः पुनः ।           Nāḍī     tu     daśa-pañcāśat-palaṃ

                                                            paśyati. [1]

                                                            proceeds until it is seen by [the smallest
                                                            unit of] time. [1]
                                                            [Explanatory note: 1 nāḍī = 60 palas; 1
                                                            pala = 60 vipalas. A nāḍī equals 24 min-
                                                            utes of modern time.]

Aryabhata’s Revolutionary Discovery — Earth’s Rotation
    पूवार्परिदग्गुल्मानं िक्षितजद्देशप्रयोगै यर्ुक्तं च ।                                 Pūrvāpara-dig-gulmānaṃ     kṣitija-
    उन्मेषलं भवे त् तद् द्वयमुद्धतं यत्र िदवसिनशोः ॥                                      deśa-prayogair yuktaṃ ca.
                                                                                          Unmeṣalaṃ bhavet tad dvayam
                                                                                          uddhataṃ yatra divasa-niśoḥ.

                                                                                          Translation:
                                                                                          That which appears as the motion of the
                                                                                          stars from east to west is in truth the Earth’s
                                                                                          own rotation. The Earth, spherical in
                                                                                          shape, rotates upon its axis from west to
                                                                                          east.
    स्थलस्य गितमाहुवर्ै खगोलस्थानभूिम्न च ।                                               Sthalasya gatim āhur vai khagola-
    यतः प्रवृित्तस्तस्यान्तो िवपयार्सो यतः स्मृतः ॥                                       sthāna-bhūmni ca.
                                                                                          Yataḥ pravr̄ttis tasyānto viparyāso
                                                                                          yataḥ smr̄taḥ.

                                                                                          Translation:
                                                                                          They say the motion of the Earth is in the
                                                                                          place of the celestial sphere. The end of its
                                                                                          rotation [causes] the reversal [of apparent
                                                                                          motion].
                                                                                          [Explanatory note: This is one of the most
                                                                                          remarkable verses in the history of science.
                                                                                          Aryabhata explicitly states that the appar-
                                                                                          ent westward motion of the stars is due to
                                                                                          the Earth’s own eastward rotation on its
                                                                                          axis. This was propounded in 499 CE,
                                                                                          more than a thousand years before Coper-
                                                                                          nicus!]

On the Earth’s Rotation
    पृिथव्याः स्वगितकारणात् खगोलस्य िस्थरत्वं                                             Due to the Earth’s own motion, the celes-
    भाित। यथा नौकायां िस्थतः पुरुषः तीरे वृक्षान्                                         tial sphere appears stationary. Just as a
    िवचिलतान् मन्यते तथा पृिथव्यां िस्थताः                                                man standing on a moving boat thinks the
    स्थलजीवाः खगोलं िवचिलतं मन्यन्ते ।                                                    trees on the bank are moving, so creatures
                                                                                          standing on the Earth think the heavens are
                                                                                          moving.

                                                                                          [Explanatory note: This analogy of the
                                                                                          boat and trees is one of the most cele-
                                                                                          brated in scientific literature. Aryabhata
                                                                                          used it to explain why we do not perceive
                                                                                          the Earth’s rotation. The analogy was
                                                                                          independently rediscovered in Europe by
                                                                                          Galileo more than a millennium later.]




                                                             ॥ इित चतुथर्पादः समाप्तः ॥
                                                            End of the Fourth Chapter

Epilogue / उपसं हार
एवं चतुष्पादसं युक्तिमदं ग्रन्थं समाप्तम् ।                               Thus this book, consisting of four chapters,
आयर्भटे न कृतिमदं गिणतज्योितषशास्त्रस्य                                   is completed. This compendium of math-
सारसङ्ग्रहः।                                                              ematics and astronomy was composed by
                                                                          Aryabhata.


Summary of Aryabhata’s Contributions

 1. Value of π: π ≈ 3.1416 (accurate to 4 decimal places)

 2. Sine Table: 24 sines at intervals of 3◦ 45′ , with radius = 3438′

 3. Kuṭtaka: General method for solving linear Diophantine equations ax + by = c

 4. Earth’s Rotation: Explicit statement that Earth rotates on its axis

 5. Spherical Earth: Earth is a sphere floating freely in space

 6. Eclipses: Correct explanation of solar and lunar eclipses

 7. Astronomical Constants: Accurate orbital periods for all planets

(१९३०) इत्यने न सं स्कृतस्य आङ्ग्लभाषायां                                 recognized by the scholar W.E. Clark,
अनुवादं कृतवन्तः।                                                         who published a Sanskrit-English edition
                                                                          in 1930. This bilingual edition follows
                                                                          Clark’s translation style while presenting
                                                                          the original Devanagari text alongside.

                                            Translator’s Preface
This bilingual edition presents Bhāskara II’s Bījagaṇita (“Seed Computation”) in parallel Sanskrit-English columns.
The text is based on the Benares Sanskrit Series edition of 1927, edited by Sudhākara Dvivedī with additional notes
by Muralīdhara Jha.
   Key Terminology:

  • बीज (bīja) — seed, origin; hence algebra

  • अव्यक्त (avyakta) — unseen, unknown quantity

  • यावत्तावत् (yāvat-tāvat) — “as much as,” the unknown x

  • रूप (rūpa) — absolute number, constant term

  • वणर् (varṇa) — colour, representing different unknowns

  • करणी (karaṇī ) — surd, irrational quantity

  • समीकरण (samīkaraṇa) — equation (making equal)

  • धन (dhana) — positive (wealth)

  • ऋण (ṛṇa) — negative (debt)

     The left column presents the original Sanskrit in Devanāgarī script. The right column provides the English trans-
lation with IAST transliteration of key terms.

Introduction / ����������

���������                                               English Translation
                                         ����������     This volume contains Part II of the Bījagaṇita (“Seed
                                                        Computation,” i.e., Algebra) composed by Bhāskara II
                                     ,                  (1114–1185 CE). The Bījagaṇita is the foundational
                                               –        treatise of Indian algebra, treating equations, unknown
                                                   —    quantities, and their solutions. Pages 58–114 encompass
                 ,                                  ,   four principal chapters: equations with one unknown,
                     ,                                  equations with unknown squares, equations with many
                                                        unknowns, and variations of the elimination method.

                                                        A distinctive feature of Bhāskara’s exposition is that
                                  (      )          ,   each topic is introduced by a verse (sūtra) containing a
                      (worked examples)                 rule, followed by worked examples (udāharaṇa) and
               यावत्तावत् (“as much as”)           ,    detailed commentary (vārttika) showing the method of
            या      याव                      ������     solution step by step. The unknown quantity is denoted
(elimination/equation)                                  by यावत्तावत् (yāvattāvat, “as much as”), abbreviated या or
                                                        याव. Equations are solved by the process of
                                                        sama-śodhana (making equal and clearing).

������� ������� —                                       Key Methods treated in this part include: (1) The
     :   ( ) �������������� (cyclic method) —           Cakravāla (cyclic) method — Bhāskara’s greatest
������������ (x2 − N y 2 = 1)                           algorithmic achievement for solving vargaprakṛti
                              ; ( ) ������������        (x2 − N y 2 = 1, Pell’s equation); (2) The Bhāvita
—                           ; ( ) ����������� —         method for product equations; (3) Madhyamāharaṇa —
                                                        the elimination method for equations with multiple
                                                        unknowns.

Chapter I: Equations with One Unknown
एकवणर्समीकरणम् ∥ Ekavarṇa-samīkaraṇa

अ                                   ����������                 Now, equations with one unknown. Here, a single
               ,                                               unknown quantity, called yāvattāvat (यावत्तावत् , “as much
                              —������������ (accepting         as”), is postulated. Combining it with known quantities
side)        ��������� (giving side)                           (rūpa, रूप), one forms an equation and determines the
                                                               value of the unknown. Each side of the equation is called
                                                               either the accepting side (what is received) or the giving
                                                               side (what is given). By the process of equal-clearing
                                                               (sama-śodhana), the value is determined.


Simple Linear Equation ∥ ����������������

��������       —                                               Example — Here, the price of a horse is unknown; let its
यावत्तावत्                   या १                              value be one yāvattāvat, written yā 1. If the price of
                                                               one horse equals the price of so many goats, then the
                                                  या ६         price in coins is determined. For one horse: yā 6.
                                                    या ६ रूप   Adding twenty coins (rūpa), the first person’s wealth
२०                           या १०                             becomes: yā 6, rūpa 20. The price of ten horses is yā 10.
                                         या १० रूप १००         Adding one hundred coins, the second person’s wealth
                                                               becomes: yā 10, rūpa 100.

��������      —                                                Equal-clearing — These two are made equal for
               —                                               clearing:

                     न्यासः---या ६ रूप २०                                   Setting down: yā 6, rūpa 20
                         या १० रूप १००                                            yā 10, rūpa 100

�����                    —                                     Rule — One should clear the unknown from one side,
                                                               and the known from the other side. When cleared, the
                                                               remainder on the other side is rūpa 400. Then, dividing
                                        या ४                   rūpa 400 by the coefficient of the unknown (yā 4), the
                                                               value of one yāvattāvat is obtained as 100. Thus the price
                                                               of one horse is 100 (coins).

Example: Jewels and Wealth / �����������������

      म◌ािणक्यामल्नीलमौिक्तकिकिमितः पञ्चाषसममा—                                   Verse 3: Jewels and Equal Wealth
      दे कस्यान्यतरस्य सप्त नव पट् तद्दलसं ख्या सखे ।
      रूपाणां नवितिद्वषिष्ठनर्योस्तौ तुल्यिवत्तौ तथा     “The measures of ruby, sapphire, pearl, and emerald of
      वीजं प्रितरुज्ञािन कुरुते मौल्यािन शीघ्रं वद ॥३॥   one are fifty, seven, nine, and half that number, O friend.
                                                         Their total wealth is one hundred sixty-two coins each.
                                                         Tell me quickly the prices, O algebraist, that make them
                                                         equal.”
                                                         Solution: Let the prices of ruby etc. be yā(1) 3, yā 2, yā
                                                         1. The two sides become:

                                                                        yā 19, yā 16, yā 7, rūpa 90
                                                                        yā 21, yā 18, yā 6, rūpa 62

                                                         By equal-clearing, the value of yāvattāvat is 4. The prices
                                                         of jewels are 12, 8, 4.

      एको द्वीित मम िद्विह शतं धने न                                                Verse 4: The Merchant’s Wealth
      त्वत्तो भवािम िह सखे िद्वगुणस्ततोऽस्यः।
      भूते द्वयोयर्दिस वै नम बहुगुणोऽहं                  “If you give me one hundred, O friend, I become twice as
      त्वत्तस्तयोवर्द धने मम िंक प्रमाणे ॥४॥             rich as you. But if I give you two hundred, I become
                                                         some multiple. Tell me, what are our respective
                                                         measures of wealth?”
                                                         Solution: Let the two merchants’ wealth be yā 1 and yā
                                                         1. After giving 100, the first becomes twice the second:
                                                         yā 1, rūpa 100 = yā 2, rūpa 200. By clearing: yā 4,
                                                         rūpa 300, whence yā = 75. The wealths are 40 and 170.

The Lotus and the Swallow / ���������������

��������        —                                          Example: The Lotus and the Swallow — Here, the
                                                           difference of the two root-measures, multiplied by the
                                                           product of the multiplier, equals the second root-wealth.
                                                           The multiplier of the second is 2. If the first root-wealth
                                                           equals the product of one multiplier and the second
                                                           root-wealth, divided by the square of the difference, then
                                                           the difference of measures is 4. Thus the first and second
                                                           root-wealths are 8 and 4, yielding a result of 2.

      एकक्रान्तचर्यनात् फलस्य वगर्ं िवशोध्य पिरिशष्यम् ।                                   Verse 8: The Lotus Problem
      पञ्चक्रान्ते न दत्तं तुल्यः कालः फले च तथै ः ॥८॥
                                                           “Having subtracted the square of the result from the first
                                                           increased [quantity], the remainder, divided by five,
                                                           gives equal time and result.”
                                                           Solution: The multiplier is 5. Dividing by the decreased
                                                           multiplier (4), the square of the small difference (16)
                                                           divides the second wealth, yielding 4. Adding the square
                                                           of the difference gives the first wealth as 20. By the rule
                                                           of proportion, time = 20.

Four Merchants with Equal Wealth / ������� ����� ������

      म◌ािणक्याणु किणनीलादीनां मुक्ताफलानां शतं                             Verse 2: Four Merchants of Equal Wealth
      षड् भािग च पञ्च रत्नवीरां ये षां चतुणार्ं धनम् ।
      सं ग्रहे हयरै न ते िनजधनाद्वेकैक िमथो               “Of rubies, coral, sapphires, pearls, and emeralds, there
      जातास्तुल्यधनाः पृथग्वद सखे तद्दनमै ल्यािन मे ॥२॥   are one hundred; six parts and five jewels. Four
                                                          merchants whose wealth, when one gives to another,
                                                          they become equal. Tell me separately, O friend, the
                                                          prices of their wealth.”
                                                          Method: The unknowns are postulated as yāvattāvats.
                                                          After four equal-clearings, the root is obtained by
                                                          intelligent reasoning. As Bhāskara himself says:
                                                                “Neither squared nor unsquared is the seed;
                                                                seeds are not separate. Intelligence alone is
                                                                the seed, for endless are the suppositions.”

Equations with Unknown Squares / ����������������������

������� —                                                                 Rule (Verses 1–2): —
      अव्यक्तवगार्िद यदा द्वयोः पक्षौ तदै केन िनःशे षं िंकिचत् ।                       When unknown squares appear on both sides,
      क्षे पं तयोरे न पदप्रदः स्याद्व्यक्तः सहे त परे न भूयः ॥१॥              divide by something to make one side a perfect square.
                                                                                              The additive must be such that it yields
      व◌्यक्तस्य मूलस्य समीकृते समव्यक्तमानं बहु लभ्यते                         a rational root when combined with the known term.
      तत् ।
      न िनवर्हेत् चे द्धनवगर्योस्त्वे ित तदा क्षे पिमदं स्यबुद्ध्या ॥२॥                        When the root of the known is equated,
                                                                                             many unknown values may be obtained;
                                                                                                         if the square does not succeed,
                                                                                           then by intelligence determine the additive.

      अव्यक्तमूलकार्ं क ततोऽस्य व्यक्तस्य पक्षस्य पदं यिद                 Verse 3:
      स्यात् ।
      मूलं धनं तथा िवधाय साव्यमव्यक्तमानं िद्वधा किल्पतं                             If the root of the unknown side, having a number,
      स्यात् ॥३॥                                                                                when made the root of the known side—
                                                                                             having made that root positive or negative,
                                                                                          the unknown value is to be assumed twofold.

Example: Series of Numbers / �������������������

      स◌्वाधर्पञ्चाशनवमै युर्क्ताः के स्युः समाश्रयाः।                  Verse 14: Numbers with Fractional Relations
      अन्यै द्वार्दशहीनाख्य पिरिशष्टाख्य तान् वद ॥१४॥
                                                         “What numbers, when increased by their own half,

                       (product)                                     two unknown quantities. When the product of two
                                            ,      ������������      unknowns appears in an equation, the bhāvita method is
                                                                     applied. The principal application of this method is in
������������                     ��������           (composition)    the bhāvanā (composition) operation for solving the
                                                                     vargaprakṛti.

���������� —            (a, b, k)                 (A, B, K)          The Bhāvanā Rule: If (a, b, k) and (A, B, K) are two
                            ,                   a2 − N b2 = k        solutions of the vargaprakṛti, i.e., a2 − N b2 = k and
A2 − N B 2 = K,                                                  :   A2 − N B 2 = K, then by bhāvanā a new solution is

           x = aA ± N bB,        y = aB ± Ab

                                                                     Special Case: When k = K = 1, the product kK = 1,
                                                                     so the composed solution directly solves x2 − N y 2 = 1.
                                                                     When k = K = −1, then kK = 1 again, so two
                                                                     solutions with additive −1 compose to a solution with
                                                                     additive +1. This is the key to terminating the Cakravāla
                                                                     method.

Introduction
This volume presents the final portion of Bhāskara II’s Bījagaṇita, comprising pages 115–170 of the original
Chowkhamba Sanskrit Series edition. This section covers the most advanced topics in the treatise:

   1. Aneka-varṇa-madhyamāharaṇa-bhedāḥ (Equations with Multiple Unknowns) — systematic methods for
      solving equations involving several unknown quantities, building on the single-variable equations treated
      earlier.
   2. Bhāvitam (Product Equations) — equations involving products of unknowns, including the famous “Bhāvita”
      (product) class of problems.
   3. Śeṣaṇa and Prakṣepaka-vidhi — special algebraic methods for remainder problems and the method of
      addition/substitution.
   4. Concluding Verses — the epilogue (upasaṃhāra) in which Bhāskara summarizes his work and pays homage
      to tradition.

    Bhāskara employs his characteristic notation where unknown quantities are denoted by the initial syllable
याव (yāva-, from yāvattāvat, “as much as”), and coefficients are prefixed to these symbols. The final sections also
include a publisher’s catalogue listing the many Sanskrit texts available from the Chowkhamba Sanskrit Book
Depot, Varanasi.



1 From the Varga-prakṛti Section (p. 115)
The opening of this portion continues the discussion of the Varga-prakṛti (square-nature) equation, i.e., equa-
tions of the form N x2 + k = y 2 . The text presents further rules and examples for finding solutions to such
indeterminate equations.

Continuation of the Square-nature Method
      समशोधने हृते पक्षौ यावच्चावत्तावकस्य रूपं प्रिक्षप्य प्रथमपक्षमूलं या २ रू १ ।
      परपक्षस्य काव १२ रू १ । वगर्प्रकृत्या मूले क २ उचे ७ वा क २८ उचे ९७ ।
      किनष्ठं कालकमानम् । उिच्चष्टस्य या २ रू १ समं हृत्वा लब्धं यावच्चावकमानम् ३ वा ४८ ।
      स्वच्छाने नोत्थापने हृते जाती राशी १, ५ वा २०, ७६ इत्यािद ॥

    Rule 6: “When the second side exists [and is not unity], having made [the two sides] equal, multiplying and
reducing, the remainder [is obtained]; having multiplied the residue by the lesser [root], dividing by the square
[nature], the reduced [equation is obtained]. Then having multiplied by the square of the lesser [root], the residue —
from that, as before, the remainder.” Thus the meaning.

Summary Rule (p. 115 bottom)
The section concludes with a general procedure:

       एवं बहुधा बुिद्धमत्त्विविचन्त्यािमित सवर्मुपपन्नम् ॥

    “Thus in many ways, by the thoughtful application of intelligence, all [is demonstrated].” Everything is proved.


2 Aneka-varṇa-madhyamāharaṇa-bhedāḥ (pp. 116–133)
This is the largest section of the final portion, dealing systematically with equations involving multiple unknown
quantities (aneka-varṇa, “many colours”). The Sanskrit term varṇa (colour) is the traditional designation for an
unknown quantity in Indian algebra — different unknowns being assigned different colours.

2.1 General Rules for Multiple Unknowns (pp. 116–117)
       अथ सूत्रं साध्ये ऽस्तु ॥
       (१) िद्वतीयपक्षे सित सममे व तु हत्यापवत्यार्े न पदे प्रसाध्ये ।
       उिच्चष्टं किनष्ठेन तदा िनहत्याच्छे दं वगर्े ण हतोऽपवतर्ः ॥ ६ ॥
       किनष्ठवगर्े ण तदा िनहत्योिच्चष्टं ततः पूवर्वदे व शे षम् ।
       इत्यथार्त् ॥

Worked Example 2 (p. 117)
        उदाहरणम् ॥
        कयोः स्यादन्तरे वगार्ै वगर्योगो ययोघर्नः ।
        तौ राशी कथयािमत्रो वहुधा बोज्ञिवत्तम ॥ २ ॥

    Example 2: “Two numbers whose difference of squares [equals] the sum of their squares — tell me those numbers,
O friend, in many ways, O best of algebraists.”

[unknown]…”

    “The difference of squares having a residue equal to the divisor, divided by the additive, then by the quotient,

thus [proceeding]…”


3 Bhāvitam and Prakṣepaka-vidhi (pp. 134–152)
3.1 Equations with Product Terms (pp. 134–138)
This section deals with bhāvita (product) equations, where the unknowns appear in product form. The method
extends the techniques for multiple unknowns to handle more complex algebraic structures.
Bijaganita – Bilingual Edition (Sanskrit-English)                                                                                        6


       अथ वा स्वणर्कल्पनायां मन्दबुद्धीनां पुनः िकिञ्चत् पिठतः ।
       तत् सूचयािम ॥
       हरमका यस्य हृित सूक्ष्मित सोऽिप िद्वतीयपदयुतातः ।
       ते नाहतोऽस्यवणार्े रूपपदे नािन्वतः कल्पः ॥ १६ ॥

   Rule 16: “The divisor multiplied by [some quantity] whose [result] is fine, added to the second term; having
multiplied by that, the unknown [is obtained], combined with a root term [as] the assumption.”

Worked Example (p. 137)
       उदाहरणम् ॥
       न यिद पदं रूपाणां िशष्ये त्तं ते न हरतोऽिप ।
       नावच्छद्गुणो भवित न चे देवमिप िकल तथै ॥ १७ ॥

      हरमितः । यस्याङ्कस्य हृितहरमका सती सूक्ष्यतीित िनश्शे षा भवित अिप च सोऽप्यङ्को हयार्े रूपपदे न च गुिणतो हरमकः सन् सूक्ष्यित तदा
ते नाहतोऽस्यवणर्स्ते न रूपाणां घनमूलं न लभ्यते तदा ते न रूपे षु हरतोऽिप तावद्गुणो भवे त् तन्मूलं रूपपदं स्यात् ।

3.2 The Bhāvita Rule (pp. 140–141)
       भािवतम् ॥
       वणर्द्वयाितकूपे ऽस्य मकरवे ष्टनै कतः ।
       एताम्या सं युताबुिद्ध कल्पयो वर्ै च्छया च तौ ॥ ३ ॥
       वणर्द्वयो वगर्योरन्ते िक्रयते ते िवपयर्यात् ।
       समयोः पक्षयोरे कमाध्यिमकमपास्य तौ वणार्ै रूपािण च

    The section on “Product”: “Two unknowns, their product having a coefficient, from one side having a single
enclosure [i.e., bracketed], having assumed any sum of their values, [proceeding] with the pair of unknowns reversed,
[taking] the square of two unknowns, the means [being] equal, having removed one middle term, the two unknowns
and the roots…”

3.3 The Method of Mean Elimination (pp. 145–147)
       माध्यमािवगमः ॥
       आसन्नमानस्य हराशमानम् अप्रािप्तगुण्ये सिहते क्षे पेण ।
       पूणर्े स्याताम् अन्तररािशकाभ्यां तदा हरां शो भवतीश्रमस्य ॥ १ ॥
       आसन्नमानयोरन्तरमे व भवे त् ।
       अं शस्थाने सदा रूपं िचन्त्ये त तथा धीमता ॥ २ ॥
       सवर्े षामासन्नमाने षु हरां शो भवित षट् ।
       तथोत्तरोत्तरं सूक्ष्मतामासन्नािन भविन्त िह ॥ ३ ॥
Bijaganita – Bilingual Edition (Sanskrit-English)                                                                      7


    The method of mean-elimination: “The divisor-measure of the approximate value, added to the non-obtained
quantity and the additive, being complete by two numbers with difference, then the divisor-fraction [gives] the
effort. The difference of two approximate values alone [suffices]. The numerator [is] always unity [at first], thus
by the intelligent. For all approximate values, the divisor-fraction is six. Thus gradually, more and more subtle
approximate values are obtained.”

Concluding Verses of the Bhāvitam Section (pp. 151–152)
      तथा गोले मयोक्तम् ।
      उत्थ सदसतां मतार्नां वै रािशकमात्रमे व पाठो बुिद्धरे व बीजम् ।
      तथा गोलाख्याय मयोक्तम् ।
      अिस्त वै रािशकं पाठी बीजं च िवमला मितः ।
      िकमन्यत् सुखदीनामतो मन्दाऽथर्मुच्यते ॥
      गणककमार्न्तरमयं बाललोचनगम्यं
      सकलगिणतसारं सोपपिट्टप्रकारम् ।
      इित बहुगुणयुक्तं सवर्दोषै र्िवमुक्तं
      पठ पठ मितबुद्धयै् लाघवं प्रौिढिसद्ध्यै ॥

     The epilogue: “Thus I have spoken of the sphere. For people ascending from the unreal to the real, the mere
reading [of this text] is the seed of intelligence. Thus I have spoken of the sphere called ‘Gola’. There is the study of
the text and pure intellect — what else [is needed]? For the delight of the wise, this is declared. This work accessible
to the eye of a child [yet] profound, the essence of all mathematics with proofs endowed, endowed with many virtues,
free from all faults — read, read with intelligence and understanding, for ease and the attainment of maturity.”

      इित श्रीभास्कराचायर्िवरिचते िसद्धान्तिशरोमणौ
      बीजगिणताध्यायः समाप्तः ॥

    “Thus ends the Bījagaṇita-adhyāya in the Siddhāntaśiromaṇi composed by Śrī Bhāskarācārya.”

4 Final Sections and Publisher’s Catalogue (pp. 153–170)
4.1 Navīna-mati-viśeṣaḥ (pp. 153–157)
The section on “Special Methods for New Understanding” presents advanced techniques for solving equations
through approximation and iteration, building on the methods developed earlier.

      नवीनमितिवशे षः ॥
      िनरक्ष पदं यद्िद्वगुणात् स्यात् फलाथर्ं धनाथर्ं तदे वात्र शे षं तदस्यम् ।
      पदद्वयं धनं शे षहृतप्रमन्यत् फलं तद्भवत् शे षमूलं धने न ॥ १ ॥
      धनाथर्ं नवं तस्य कृत्या िवहीनो गुणः शे षमकोऽस्यवणर्स्य मानम् ।
      मूद्गुसेव मते यदा शे षमानं भवे द्िद्वतीयं तदा लिव्धतौ ते ॥ २ ॥
Bijaganita – Bilingual Edition (Sanskrit-English)                                                                    8


    Rule 1: “A number, when doubled, becomes the root; for the fruit [result], for wealth [coefficient], that same
residue here — its two terms [are] the wealth divided by the residue; the fruit [is] the root of the residue multiplied
by the wealth. The new wealth is diminished by nine times its square; the multiplier, diminished [thus], [gives] the
measure of the unknown. When by the opinion of Mūdgu [i.e., by the method of approximation], the residue-value
becomes the second [term], then the quotient for both.”

4.3 The Method of Approximate Roots (pp. 160–165)
This section presents the āsanna-mūla (approximate root) method — an iterative technique for finding succes-
sively better approximations to irrational square roots, a precursor to what is now known as Newton’s method.

      आसन्नमूलािन सूत्रािण ॥
      आसन्नमानस्य हराशमानम् अप्रािप्तगुण्ये सिहते क्षे पेण ।
      पूणर्े स्याताम् अन्तररािशकाभ्यां तदा हरां शो भवतीश्रमस्य ॥ १ ॥
                                                                                          √
    The mathematical procedure is as follows: given a non-square number n, to find            n:
   1. Choose an initial approximation a1 (the “approximate value”)

   2. Compute the residue: r = n − a21
                                                           r
   3. Form the next approximation: a2 = a1 +
                                                          2a1
   4. Iterate for successively better approximations

    “There is the study of this work and pure intellect — what else [is needed]? Thus is declared for the delight of
the wise. This [work], accessible as a child’s play [yet] the essence of all mathematics with demonstrations, endowed
with many virtues, free from all faults — read, read with intelligence and understanding, for ease and the attainment
of maturity.”

    The author reflects on the completion of the work:

      तथा गोले मयोक्तम् ।

      तथा गोलाख्याय मयोक्तम् ॥

    “Thus I have spoken of the sphere. For people ascending from the unreal to the real, the mere reading [of this
text] is the seed of intelligence. Thus I have spoken of what is called the sphere.”

पूणार्ङ्केषु, िभन्ने षु, अनुपाते षु, व्याजे षु, क्षे त्रफले षु, घनफले षु, श्रे णीषु   bhāratīyagaṇitasya     sarvādhikaprasiddhapāṭhyapus-
च गिणतिवषयान् व्यवस्थापयित।                                                           takam asti |
                                                                                      The Līlāvatī is the first section of Bhāskara II’s mon-
                                                                                      umental work Siddhāntaśiromaṇi, composed in 1150
                                                                                      CE. Named after Bhāskara’s daughter, it is the most
                                                                                      celebrated textbook of Indian arithmetic. The work
                                                                                      covers the entire field of elementary mathematics:
                                                                                      arithmetic operations with integers and fractions, rules
                                                                                      of proportion, interest calculation, plane geometry, solid
                                                                                      geometry, and combinatorial problems.

िमश्रप्रश्नाः, क्षे त्रव्यवहारः, खातव्यवहारः, िचितव्यवहारः, छायाव्यवहारः,             vargamūlam, ghanaḥ,ghanamūlam — eteṣāṃ parikar-
